headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to bear the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed to residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Dominion Energy, Governor Abigail Spanberger, residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, State Senator Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling.
opponents: Data Center Coalition, data center operators.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Dominion-Backed Bills, Directing Regulators to Assign Electricity Costs to Data Centers
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 1393, which directs the State Corporation Commission to ensure data centers pay their fair share for electricity generation and distribution costs. This aims to prevent these expenses from being unfairly passed on to residential customers, who have seen bills increase due to data center demand.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water users providing water to data centers report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board on a monthly basis.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Potomac Conservancy, Nature Forward, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Del. Liz Guzman.
news_headline: Data centers are drinking our Potomac River region resources up. Our team is fighting for transparency in Virginia
news_summary: The Potomac Conservancy is advocating for SB 553 to mandate data centers report water usage to the State Water Control Board, citing concerns about the region's water supply failing to meet needs by 2030 due to data center sprawl and lack of transparency. This bill is seen as critical for environmental and water advocates to accurately assess and combat the impact of data centers.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high-energy data centers, examining noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allowing for assessments of water, agricultural, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups, localities, Delegate Joshua Thomas.
news_headline: 'They just don't fit': Virginia Beach moves to restrict 'hyperscale' data centers
news_summary: Virginia Beach City Council is considering a ban or strict restrictions on large-scale data centers due to concerns about land use, infrastructure demands, and noise. This local action reflects broader statewide issues addressed by HB 153, which empowers localities to require site assessments for noise and other impacts.
